title: The Ackermann function

based_on.title: Ackermann’s Function Is Not Primitive Recursive

summary: Construct a total computable function whose diagonal exceeds every primitive-recursive function, while each fixed row remains primitive recursive.
abstract: Addition, multiplication and exponentiation can all be built by primitive recursion, where a specified input determines how many recursive steps are taken. Does every algorithm that always finishes admit such a construction? The Ackermann function gives a concrete negative answer. Its first rows are successor, addition by two, a linear function and an exponential function, and every fixed row is still primitive recursive. A single algorithm can compute all the rows, yet their diagonal eventually exceeds every primitive-recursive unary function. Comparing the growth of these rows proves that total computability is strictly broader than primitive recursiveness and explains why a separate finite construction for each fixed parameter need not give one primitive-recursive function of all the parameters.
